response: {"title":"Changed-dependency test ordering","intervention":"Order available verification checks by estimated failure-detection value per minute for the changed modules and their direct dependents, execute them in that order, and stop launching new checks when the remaining deadline equals the longest already-observed check duration.","claim":"Compared with no appended instruction, this instruction will raise hidden-test pass_rate on multi-module Python tasks without increasing deadline-miss frequency under the same fixed deadline.","mechanism":"Ranking tests by expected diagnostic yield divided by runtime concentrates bounded verification time on likely regression surfaces, while the observed-duration stop rule prevents a final test from consuming the completion margin.","assumptions":["The agent can map changed modules to direct dependents.","Past check durations observed within the task are useful bounds for subsequent checks.","Available checks differ meaningfully in failure-detection value and runtime."],"risks":["Failures in distant dependents may be deprioritized.","The first observed check can be unrepresentatively short and produce an unsafe stopping margin.","Estimating detection value may consume time or encode poor guesses.","A slow but essential full-suite check may never run."],"test_plan":{"experiment":"Randomize matched multi-module Python tasks between this appended instruction and no appended instruction, holding model, tools, deadline, and task order constant; evaluate hidden tests after each run and record deadline completion.","metrics":["pass_rate","wall_time","turns"],"success_condition":"The instruction arm has higher pass_rate with deadline-miss frequency no greater than control; report wall_time and turns as secondary efficiency outcomes."},"single_shot_ordinal":2}
